Mutable pass counts and package-linter results are omitted from this lesson.

### Deliberate limits

This operation recovers only the rotational block of a logarithm. A complete $SE(3)$ logarithm must also recover the finite linear exponential-coordinate block from the transformation's translation. The selected principal rotation vector is discontinuous across the exact-$\pi$ branch boundary even though the represented orientation changes continuously. `Rotation3` does not encode frame labels or angle units, so callers must preserve the frame interpretation and treat the returned components as radians.

## Algorithm summaries for the $SO(3)$ exponential and principal logarithm {#sec-spatial-kernel-so3-exp-log-algorithms}

This section condenses the two preceding implementations into mathematical pseudocode. Each line performs one algorithmic assignment or decision using the mathematical quantity itself. A monospaced name in square brackets gives the corresponding C++ identifier; for example, $\theta\,[\mathtt{theta}]$ means that the mathematical angle $\theta$ is stored in the C++ variable `theta`.

### Exponential: rotation vector to rotation matrix

The exponential receives ${}^{a}\boldsymbol\phi\in\mathbb R^3$ in radians and returns a `Rotation3` storing $\mathbf R\in SO(3)$. The complete algorithm is

$$
\begin{aligned}
&\textbf{input:}
&&{}^{a}\boldsymbol\phi
\in\mathbb R^3\ \mathrm{rad}
\ [\mathtt{rotation\_vector}],
\quad \mathtt{policy},\\
&\textbf{output:}
&&\mathbf R\in SO(3)
\ [\mathtt{rotation\_matrix}],\\[2pt]
&\theta\ [\mathtt{theta}]
&&\gets
\left\|{}^{a}\boldsymbol\phi\right\|_2,\\
&\textbf{if }\theta=0,
&&\textbf{return }\mathbf I_3.
\end{aligned}
$$

For $\theta>0$, the algorithm continues with the coefficient selection and Rodrigues' formula:

$$
\begin{aligned}
&A_{\mathrm{eval}}(\theta)
\ [\mathtt{coefficient\_a}]
&&\gets
\begin{cases}
1-\dfrac{\theta^2}{6}
+\dfrac{\theta^4}{120}
-\dfrac{\theta^6}{5040},
&0<\theta\leq\theta_{\mathrm{series}},\\[6pt]
\dfrac{\sin\theta}{\theta},
&\theta>\theta_{\mathrm{series}},
\end{cases}\\[8pt]
&B_{\mathrm{eval}}(\theta)
\ [\mathtt{coefficient\_b}]
&&\gets
\begin{cases}
\dfrac12
-\dfrac{\theta^2}{24}
+\dfrac{\theta^4}{720}
-\dfrac{\theta^6}{40320},
&0<\theta\leq\theta_{\mathrm{series}},\\[6pt]
\dfrac{1-\cos\theta}{\theta^2},
&\theta>\theta_{\mathrm{series}},
\end{cases}\\[8pt]
&\boldsymbol\Phi
\ [\mathtt{rotation\_generator}]
&&\gets
[{}^{a}\boldsymbol\phi]_\times,\\
&\mathbf R
\ [\mathtt{rotation\_matrix}]
&&\gets
\mathbf I_3
+A_{\mathrm{eval}}(\theta)\boldsymbol\Phi
+B_{\mathrm{eval}}(\theta)\boldsymbol\Phi^2,\\
&\textbf{return}
&&\mathtt{Rotation3}(\mathbf R).
\end{aligned}
$$

The two polynomial branches are the evaluated sixth-order approximations used by the code. The direct branches evaluate the exact trigonometric coefficients.

### Principal logarithm: rotation matrix to rotation vector

The logarithm receives the validated $\mathbf R\in SO(3)$ stored in `matrix_` and returns the selected ${}^{a}\boldsymbol\phi$ in radians together with the numerical branch. Its complete algorithm is

$$
\begin{aligned}
&\textbf{input:}
&&\mathbf R\in SO(3)\ [\mathtt{matrix\_}],
\quad \mathtt{policy},\\
&\textbf{output:}
&&{}^{a}\boldsymbol\phi\in\mathbb R^3\ \mathrm{rad}
\ [\mathtt{rotation\_vector}],
\quad b\ [\mathtt{branch}],\\[2pt]
&c_\theta\ [\mathtt{cosine\_theta}]
&&\gets
\frac{\operatorname{tr}(\mathbf R)-1}{2},\\
&{}^{a}\mathbf u\ [\mathtt{skew\_difference}]
&&\gets
\begin{bmatrix}
R_{32}-R_{23}\\
R_{13}-R_{31}\\
R_{21}-R_{12}
\end{bmatrix},\\[8pt]
&s_\theta\ [\mathtt{sine\_theta}]
&&\gets
\frac12\left\|{}^{a}\mathbf u\right\|_2,\\
&\theta\ [\mathtt{theta}]
&&\gets
\operatorname{atan2}(s_\theta,c_\theta)
\in[0,\pi],\\
&\textbf{if }\theta=0,
&&\textbf{return }
(\mathbf 0_3,\mathtt{identity}).
\end{aligned}
$$

For a non-identity rotation, test the near-$\pi$ condition first. If it holds, begin the symmetric axis recovery:

$$
\begin{aligned}
&\textbf{if }
\pi-\theta\leq\theta_{\mathrm{near}\text{-}\pi},
&&\textbf{enter the near-}\pi\textbf{ branch:}\\[2pt]
&\quad\mathbf R_{\mathrm{sym}}
\ [\mathtt{symmetric\_part}]
&&\quad\gets
\frac12(\mathbf R+\mathbf R^{\mathsf T}),\\
&\quad d_\pi\ [\mathtt{denominator}]
&&\quad\gets 1-c_\theta,\\
&\quad\mathbf Q
\ [\mathtt{axis\_outer\_product}]
&&\quad\gets
\frac{
\mathbf R_{\mathrm{sym}}-c_\theta\mathbf I_3
}{d_\pi}
=
{}^{a}\mathbf s_\omega
({}^{a}\mathbf s_\omega)^{\mathsf T},\\[6pt]
&\quad k
&&\quad\gets
\min\!\left(
\underset{i\in\{1,2,3\}}{\operatorname{arg\,max}}
Q_{ii}
\right),\\
&\quad k_{\mathrm{Eigen}}\ [\mathtt{dominant\_index}]
&&\quad\gets k-1
\quad\text{for Eigen's zero-based index},\\
&\quad q_k\ [\mathtt{dominant\_component\_squared}]
&&\quad\gets Q_{kk},\\
&\quad d_k\ [\mathtt{dominant\_component}]
&&\quad\gets\sqrt{q_k}.
\end{aligned}
$$

With the dominant component available, complete the near-$\pi$ axis, sign, and output calculation:

$$
\begin{aligned}
&\quad{}^{a}\widetilde{\mathbf s}_\omega
\ [\mathtt{axis}]
&&\quad\gets
\frac{\mathbf Q_{:k}}{d_k},
\qquad
{}^{a}\widetilde s_{\omega,k}\gets d_k,\\
&\quad n_s\ [\mathtt{axis\_norm}]
&&\quad\gets
\|{}^{a}\widetilde{\mathbf s}_\omega\|_2,\\
&\quad{}^{a}\widetilde{\mathbf s}_\omega
&&\quad\gets
{}^{a}\widetilde{\mathbf s}_\omega/n_s,\\
&\quad\alpha\ [\mathtt{skew\_alignment}]
&&\quad\gets
({}^{a}\widetilde{\mathbf s}_\omega)^{\mathsf T}
{}^{a}\mathbf u,\\
&\quad\textbf{if }\alpha<0,
&&\quad{}^{a}\widetilde{\mathbf s}_\omega
\gets-{}^{a}\widetilde{\mathbf s}_\omega,\\
&\quad{}^{a}\boldsymbol\phi
\ [\mathtt{rotation\_vector}]
&&\quad\gets
\theta{}^{a}\widetilde{\mathbf s}_\omega,\\
&\quad\textbf{return}
&&\quad({}^{a}\boldsymbol\phi,\mathtt{near\_pi}).
\end{aligned}
$$

If the near-$\pi$ condition is false, select the small-angle or nominal recovery factor and finish through ${}^{a}\boldsymbol\phi=f(\theta){}^{a}\mathbf u$:

$$
\begin{aligned}
&\textbf{if }0<\theta\leq\theta_{\mathrm{series}}:
&&\\[-2pt]
&\quad f(\theta)\ [\mathtt{recovery\_factor}]
&&\quad\gets
\frac12+\frac{\theta^2}{12}
+\frac{7\theta^4}{720},\\
&\quad b\ [\mathtt{branch}]
&&\quad\gets\mathtt{small\_angle},\\[6pt]
&\textbf{else}:
&&\theta_{\mathrm{series}}<\theta
<\pi-\theta_{\mathrm{near}\text{-}\pi},\\
&\quad f(\theta)\ [\mathtt{recovery\_factor}]
&&\quad\gets
\frac{\theta}{2s_\theta},\\
&\quad b\ [\mathtt{branch}]
&&\quad\gets\mathtt{nominal},\\[6pt]
&{}^{a}\boldsymbol\phi
\ [\mathtt{rotation\_vector}]
&&\gets
f(\theta){}^{a}\mathbf u,\\
&\textbf{return}
&&({}^{a}\boldsymbol\phi,b).
\end{aligned}
$$

### Production checks omitted from the mathematical pseudocode

The displayed algorithms assume finite inputs, valid policy values, and a validated $\mathbf R\in SO(3)$. The C++ boundary adds the required guards without changing the mathematical branch equations: it validates the policy and input components, enforces the supported angle, rejects non-finite intermediate or output values, clamps only tolerated round-off in $c_\theta$ and $Q_{kk}$, and rejects an unrecoverable zero axis or nominal sine factor. The detailed exponential and logarithm sections above record the corresponding `GeometryError` results.

The two algorithms form inverse operations only after the logarithm's principal-domain convention is applied. For every validated $\mathbf R$,

$$
\operatorname{Exp}_{SO(3)}
\!\left(
\operatorname{Log}_{SO(3)}^{\mathrm{principal}}(\mathbf R)
\right)
=
\mathbf R,
$$

whereas $\operatorname{Log}_{SO(3)}^{\mathrm{principal}}(\operatorname{Exp}_{SO(3)}({}^{a}\boldsymbol\phi))={}^{a}\boldsymbol\phi$ requires ${}^{a}\boldsymbol\phi$ to lie inside the selected principal domain, including the canonical sign at $\theta=\pi$.
